A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EM-LLM, with matching authors, architecture, benchmarks, and retained results. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V2 reports original LongBench and ∞-Bench experiments, PG-19 segmentation measurements, human-annotation analyses, and component ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains these original results and adds surprise-segmented RAG results and retrieval-buffer-size experiments in Table 9 and Appendix D.3.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same surprise segmentation, graph refinement, and similarity/contiguity retrieval procedure. Corrected threshold notation and explanations of single-pass refinement clarify the existing method. Discussed neural and multimodal extensions are not implemented additions.

E1.justification: Both versions use LongBench, ∞-Bench, PG-19, and the same human-annotated podcast material. New experiments use retained LongBench tasks. V2 already shows retrieval across approximately 10 million tokens in Figure 1; v3's revised maximum-length statement does not establish additional coverage.

E2.justification: Table 9 adds RAG-S, using NV-Embed-v2 with EM-LLM's surprise-based segmentation, to the LLaMA-3.1 comparison. Results are provided for LongBench only. InfLLM, the original RAG configurations, full-context models, and segmentation comparators are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include dynamically retrieving surprise-segmented RAG chunks to a 1500-word budget and varying Mistral's retrieved buffer across 1K, 2K, 4K, and 6K tokens with 4K local tokens. Appendix D.3 also stratifies results by example length. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds targeted investigations of surprise segmentation within RAG and retrieval-budget sensitivity on four LongBench tasks, including analysis by context length. Existing segmentation and contiguity ablations are retained: v2 Figures 9–11 correspond to v3 Figures 11–13.

E5.justification: Appendix A.1 newly reports two-tailed z-tests, stating benchmark-level significance at p < 0.05 with a reported Phi-3.5 LongBench exception of p = 0.23. It acknowledges that most individual-task improvements are not significant. No additional seed or repeated-run information is supplied.

E6.justification: Previously reported table scores are retained. Additions include RAG-S's LongBench average of 25.89 in Table 9 and retrieval-buffer results in Table 12; QMSum scores are 23.24, 23.68, 24.47, and 24.30 for 1K, 2K, 4K, and 6K retrieved tokens. These are additional comparisons, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 replaces the O(kn) refinement derivation with chunk-based accounting yielding O(nm + n^2/k), bounded by O(nm). New Appendix C.2 separately derives attention and retrieval costs, including the growing retrieval term. The existing k-NN/softmax approximation proof moves from E.1 to F.1 unchanged.

C1.justification: V3 narrows the biological framing from human-like to human-inspired; Appendix E.1 explicitly supports this qualification by acknowledging missing evidence of actual human-like episodic processing. The introduction also updates the refinement-complexity claim. The central architectural contributions and headline empirical claims remain.

C2.justification: New Appendix E substantially qualifies the human-memory analogy, identifying non-parametric storage, missing nested events and consolidation, limited multimodal integration, and absent direct mechanistic validation. V3 also discusses the lack of refinement-convergence guarantees, hypothesizes why RAG-S underperforms, and explains the limited scope of the buffer-size study.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code-repository link and substantial parameter-selection documentation in Appendix D.1: model-specific gamma choices, their selection using LongBench, one neighboring event on either side, the selected contiguity ratio of 0.3, and token-budget interpretation. These disclose existing experimental choices; hardware and offloading information was already present.

R1.justification: Appendix E substantially expands positioning against differentiable and associative memory approaches, including SEM, Hopfield networks, Neural Turing Machines, differentiable neural computers, and MERLIN. It newly relates refinement to Louvain and adds multimodal connections. The Newman fast-community-detection citation supporting the old complexity argument is removed.

P1.justification: V3 substantially expands structured exposition through parameter-selection guidance and a five-part discussion appendix. It rewrites the introduction around labeled Contributions and Performance paragraphs, changes human-like terminology to human-inspired, and reorganizes appendices C–F. The main section sequence remains intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds complexity Figures 9–10 and buffer-analysis Figure 14/Table 12, expands Table 9 with RAG-S, and adds task categories to Table 3. Existing figures are retained with relocation, renumbering, and limited caption or legend edits; the overall visual format remains similar.

improvement.justification: V3 improves reproducibility and assessment through parameter disclosures, a code link, targeted additional experiments, and clearer computational-cost accounting. Its explicit human-inspired qualification makes the biological interpretation more defensible. These are useful gains, although the new empirical evidence is limited and Appendix A.1's significance-testing procedure remains underspecified; the core experimental findings are unchanged.
